importance_ranking.reason: Significant visual variation across sub-types — cold storage PEB with insulated white panels, open-sided agricultural shed, and standard industrial warehouse are visually distinct. Buyers use the image to confirm structure type before reading any specs; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Built type, eave height, span width, and temperature control are primary shortlisting gates — a buyer needing a cold storage PEB at 10m eave height cannot evaluate a listing that does not show these specs. Specs are discovery signals, not just confirmatory.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall in this category — buyers search by spec, geography, and execution capability, not by manufacturer name; EPACK, Interarch, and ECOPlus are known but not searched by name on IndiaMART.
importance_ranking.reason: For a capital construction project, buyers evaluate seller credentials — PAN-India execution capability, IS code compliance, turnkey vs supply-only service mode, and past project portfolio — after initial spec shortlisting but before price negotiation.

Indian buyers are price-aggressive and compare per-sq-ft rates, but price is only meaningful after spec equivalence (eave height, built type, temperature control) is confirmed. Final price is always project-negotiated; listed rate is a budget entry point.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some sellers quote per kg for steel structure supply-only (without erection) — this creates real price comparison confusion when mixed with per-sq-ft turnkey listings. Unit must be shown alongside price.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per kg is a genuine market ambiguity — turnkey project sellers quote per sq ft while steel-supply-only sellers quote per kg. A buyer comparing prices without unit context will misread the comparison entirely.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the entire construction method (PEB vs RCC vs Prefab) — non-interchangeable across buyer requirements, with PEB delivering 30–50% cost and timeline advantages over RCC, making this the primary product class separator.

Cold storage vs ambient storage requires fundamentally different materials (PUF/EPS insulation, HVAC integration) and commands a 2–3x price premium — the single largest price delta within the storage buildings category.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Clear span (bay width) is a primary structural design driver — buyers specify required span (20m, 30m, 40m) to determine primary frame design and steel tonnage, and sellers cannot quote accurately without it.

Floor load and roof load specifications are required by buyers storing heavy goods (automotive parts, industrial machinery) to confirm structural adequacy — a critical design input that changes steel section sizes and cost.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Routes the RFQ to sellers with the right capability — Cold Storage requires specialised insulation and HVAC integration that most general PEB sellers cannot supply, making application the primary seller-routing signal.

Defines project scale so sellers can confirm execution capacity and provide a meaningful per-sq-ft estimate — a 1000 sq ft shed and a 50000 sq ft warehouse require entirely different fabrication and logistics capabilities.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need eave height to determine structural design feasibility and quote accurately — a 4m eave height shed and a 12m eave height industrial warehouse are fundamentally different structural projects with different steel tonnage and cost.
